mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen each of the last three weeks (-13.7 -> -13.4 -> -12.1 -> -10.9), indicating positive momentum in retail footfall recovery that should persist into the next four weeks as habitual activity patterns continue to normalize.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved in 3 of last 3 weekly transitions
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is equal to or lower than the mean over the last 28 days despite the observed monotonic three-week uptrend.

mechanism_narrative: A week-on-week rise in TRANSIT usage (from -9.4 to -5.3 over two weeks) signals increased willingness to travel outside the home for non-essential errands, which should translate into higher RETAIL_REC within the next two weeks as transit-dependent shoppers resume trips.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises above -5 points for the current week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise within two weeks of TRANSIT crossing above -5 points, or declines despite the trigger being met.

mechanism_narrative: In a reopening regime, recovering WORKPLACES mobility (improving from -9.3 to -3.7 over the last two weeks) reflects loosened restrictions on commercial activity, which should drive a broad-based increase in RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks as commercial districts reopen more fully.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next four weeks even though WORKPLACES continues its upward trajectory, or WORKPLACES reverses and RETAIL_REC still rises.

mechanism_narrative: When PARKS mobility rises while RESIDENTIAL mobility simultaneously falls, it indicates a substitution of outdoor leisure activity away from staying home, but this outdoor-oriented substitution draws discretionary trips away from indoor retail, producing a net decline in RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS and RESIDENTIAL both moved (PARKS from -13.9 to -14.6, RESIDENTIAL from 7.3 to 6.0) over last two weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises or stays flat over two weeks despite concurrent PARKS increase and RESIDENTIAL decrease, invalidating the substitution mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: The sustained negative level of PARKS mobility relative to baseline, combined with the time of year (mid-May), suggests seasonal outdoor activity is still ramping up; as warmer weather continues to draw people outdoors over the next four weeks, discretionary retail trips will be partially displaced, keeping RETAIL_REC growth muted or negative.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS remains near -14 to -17 despite overall mobility recovery
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases substantially over the next four weeks even as PARKS mobility remains depressed or continues to decline, contradicting the seasonal displacement mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has risen sharply and persistently (31.6 to 37.6 over four weeks), suggesting household shopping needs are increasingly being met through grocery/pharmacy trips rather than general retail, which could saturate near-term demand and suppress RETAIL_REC growth in the immediate next week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM exceeds +35 for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM reached 35.1 (t-1w) and 37.6 (t-0w), exceeding +35 for two weeks
regime_hint: steady state with elevated essential shopping
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises in the week immediately following two consecutive weeks of GROCERY_PHARM above +35, contradicting the saturation/substitution hypothesis.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous recovery in both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility indicates a coordinated loosening of commuting and workplace restrictions; when both series rise together, the combined restoration of commuting-linked retail opportunities (e.g., lunch and after-work shopping) amplifies RETAIL_REC growth beyond what either series alone would predict, over a four-week horizon.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both increase for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:both WORKPLACES (-9.3 to -3.7) and TRANSIT (-9.4 to -5.3) improved over the last two weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to show above-trend growth over four weeks despite both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT rising concurrently for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: In a regime where RESIDENTIAL mobility remains persistently elevated above baseline (around +6 to +7), households continue to spend more time at home than pre-pandemic, reflecting lingering caution that dampens discretionary retail outings; this residual caution should suppress RETAIL_REC recovery over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL has stayed between 6.0 and 7.3 across all four weeks
regime_hint: partial reopening with elevated residential caution
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises meaningfully over the next two weeks even though RESIDENTIAL remains at or above +6, invalidating the caution-suppression mechanism.
